circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Yas Marina Circuit is a 5. 281 km track located on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, designed by Hermann Tilke to host the season-concluding Abu Dhabi Grand Prix since 2009. The venue represents the second Middle Eastern Formula One circuit, following Bahrain's earlier establishment and preceding later additions in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: A street circuit surrounding Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb hosts the Australian Grand Prix each year as its primary Formula One event, alongside supporting racing categories and other competitions. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 classification status.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326-kilometer circuit originally operated as the Österreichring and staged the Austrian Grand Prix continuously from 1970 to 1987. After undergoing reconstruction and shortening, the track was renamed and returned to hosting the Grand Prix from 1997 to 2003.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street track in Azerbaijan's capital city, positioned along the historic boulevard, and at over 6 km per lap ranks among the longest venues on the F1 calendar. The circuit first hosted Formula One competition in 2016 as the European Grand Prix before becoming home to the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017 onwards.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit is a 5. 412 km facility that hosts the annual Formula One Grand Prix, marking the championship's inaugural Middle Eastern event. Beyond Formula One, the venue accommodates various motorsport disciplines including GP2 racing, endurance competitions, and previously featured Australian V8 Supercars from 2006 until 2010.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, Spain, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced mix of extended straights and diverse corner types that test multiple racing disciplines. The venue holds an FIA Grade 1 license and accommodates up to 140,700 spectators across its facilities.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: This Belgian circuit spans 7. 004 km through the Ardennes forest near Stavelot and hosts the Formula One Belgian Grand Prix annually since 1985, with only two exceptions in 2003 and 2006. The venue has a storied racing history dating back to 1925 and featured prominently in F1's inaugural season in 1950, making it one of the championship's longest-running Grand Prix locations.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Montreal's Notre Dame Island, this 4. 361-kilometre circuit hosts the Formula One Canadian Grand Prix annually. Beyond Formula One, the track has accommodated various other major motorsport competitions, including sportscar championships and North American racing series.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading District, the Shanghai International Circuit is a motorsport venue renowned for hosting the Chinese Grand Prix, which ran annually from 2004 to 2019 before resuming in 2024. The track has expanded its racing calendar to include the Shanghai ePrix beginning in 2024.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Located in England near villages in Northamptonshire, Silverstone Circuit has been the traditional home of the British Grand Prix since 1948 and hosted the inaugural World Championship race in 1950. After decades of alternating with other tracks, the Grand Prix became a permanent fixture at Silverstone from 1987 onwards, while the venue also regularly stages international motorcycle racing.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, a 4. 381 km track near Budapest in Mogyoród, hosted the first Formula One Grand Prix held in Eastern Europe when it opened in 1986, constructed in just eight months, faster than any other Formula One circuit. Built outside the capital near a major highway rather than as a street course through Budapest's largest park as originally planned, the inaugural race commemorated János Drapál, Hungary's pioneering motorcycle Grand Prix champion.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: The Autodromo Nazionale Monza is a 5. 793 km circuit located near Milan that has hosted the Italian Grand Prix continuously since 1949, making it one of the longest-serving Formula One venues. Constructed in 1922 as Europe's oldest purpose-built racing facility, the track earned its nickname "the Temple of Speed" through its characteristically long straights and fast-corner configurations that encourage high-velocity racing.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: The Suzuka Circuit, a 5. 807 km track situated in Mie Prefecture, Japan and operated by Honda Mobilityland, serves as a premier venue for Formula One racing and other major motorsport events. With a spectator capacity of 155,000, the facility has established itself as one of the world's most significant racing destinations.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street track located in Paradise, Nevada that snakes through the famous Las Vegas Boulevard and its surrounding streets, featuring iconic venues such as MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas as prominent landmarks along the route. The circuit traverses the heart of the Las Vegas Strip, home to the city's major hotels and casinos, creating a unique urban racing environment.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is a 4. 304 km circuit honoring brothers Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez, both of whom died in racing accidents during the 1960s and 1970s. The track has hosted Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix in multiple eras, returning to the calendar in 2015 after a 23-year absence, with the event now branded as the Mexico City Grand Prix since 2021.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit laid out around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, featuring 3. 363 miles of track with 19 corners and qualifying speeds averaging 139 mph. Designed by Apex Circuit Design specifically for Formula One, it hosts the Miami Grand Prix, which joined the championship calendar in 2022.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco stretches 3. 337 kilometers through the streets of Monte Carlo and La Condamine, hugging the harbor of the Principality of Monaco. Though officially recognized by its full name, it is widely known simply as "Monte Carlo" due to its location predominantly within that Monaco neighborhood.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: This Dutch coastal circuit in the Zandvoort dunes, situated 35 kilometers west of Amsterdam, spans 4. 259 kilometers and hosted the Dutch Grand Prix after rejoining the Formula One calendar in 2021. The track's partnership with the championship concluded after the 2026 season.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit is a Qatari racing venue situated north of Doha near the city of Lusail. Spanning 5. 419 kilometers with a 1.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos is a 4. 309 km Brazilian motorsport venue in São Paulo that opened in 1940 and was later renamed after Formula One driver José Carlos Pace, who tragically died in an aviation accident in 1977. The counterclockwise circuit features supporting facilities including a kart track dedicated to fellow Brazilian racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street track situated along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea waterfront that has been home to the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix since its debut in 2021, while also recently welcoming a Formula E event from 2025 onwards.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's Marina Bay area, incorporating sections of the Downtown Core and Kallang districts into its layout as a temporary street course.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced mix of extended straights and diverse corner types, making it a comprehensive test of driver and vehicle capability. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: Situated in Austin, Texas, the Circuit of the Americas is a 3. 426-mile FIA Grade 1 facility that serves as the permanent venue for the Formula One United States Grand Prix alongside hosting major international motorsport events including MotoGP and sports car championships. The track has previously accommodated various racing series ranging from IndyCar to rallycross competitions.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai and British motorsport competitor who represents Thailand in Formula One, currently driving for Williams.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, having claimed two world championships during his tenure with Renault in 2005 and 2006, along with 32 Grand Prix victories over his 23-season career. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso has achieved significant success in endurance racing, including victories at Le Mans and the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship, making him the sole driver to have secured both a Formula One title and a World Endurance Championship.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli made his Formula One debut in 2025 and currently races for Mercedes, where he has claimed eight Grand Prix victories.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British racing driver currently competing in Formula One with the Haas team.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Gabi Bortoleto, a Brazilian motorsport talent, currently races in Formula One as a driver for Audi.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas currently races for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from a 13-season career that includes 10 race victories. He achieved back-to-back championship runner-up finishes while driving for Mercedes in 2019 and 2020.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Alejandro Colapinto is an Argentine driver competing in Formula One's top tier for the Alpine team.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Jack Doohan, an Australian racing driver, currently competes in prototype racing while maintaining a reserve role at Haas in Formula One, where he has participated in several races during the 2024-2025 season.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently competing for Alpine. The driver previously achieved victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix while racing for AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Alexandre Hadjar is a French-Algerian driver representing France in Formula One, currently racing for Red Bull Racing.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Ferrari who has achieved seven world championship titles, equalling Michael Schumacher's record. He holds numerous all-time records in the sport, including the most career victories, pole positions, and podium finishes.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races for Audi in Formula One, bringing substantial experience from his lengthy career in the sport. Beyond single-seaters, he achieved significant success in endurance competition, notably securing victory at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson, a New Zealand motorsport competitor, currently drives for Racing Bulls in the Formula One championship.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc, a Monégasque driver competing for Ferrari, finished as championship runner-up in 2022 and has secured nine Grand Prix victories throughout his Formula One career spanning nine seasons.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen is a Danish driver who has competed across multiple racing series, including two separate stints in Formula One spanning 2014-2020 and 2022-2024. Currently, he races in the World Endurance Championship for BMW's factory team WRT and competes part-time in NASCAR's top series with Trackhouse Racing.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British driver, secured the 2025 Formula One World Drivers' Championship while racing for McLaren. Across his eight seasons in the sport, he has accumulated 13 Grand Prix victories.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Haas. The French driver achieved a Grand Prix victory at the 2021 Hungarian round while competing for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: The Mexican driver competes for Cadillac in Formula One and has secured six Grand Prix victories throughout his 15-year career in the sport. Pérez finished as championship runner-up in 2023 while driving for Red Bull.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Oscar Piastri is an Australian Formula One driver currently competing for McLaren, having secured nine Grand Prix victories throughout his four seasons in the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo, an Australian driver known by the nickname "the Honey Badger," competed in Formula One for 14 seasons between 2011 and 2024, securing eight race victories during his career.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: George Russell, a British motorsports competitor, drives for Mercedes in Formula One and has claimed seven race victories throughout his eight-season tenure in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz competes for Williams in Formula One, where he has secured four race victories during his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver currently racing in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition. He competed in Formula One during the 2023 and 2024 seasons before transitioning to endurance racing.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian Formula One driver currently racing for Aston Martin. The competitor, whose full name is Lance Jacob Strulovitch, maintains an active presence in the sport's highest racing tier.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda, a Japanese motorsport competitor, currently holds a reserve position with Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls in Formula One. Previously, he contested the championship as a full-time participant across five seasons from 2021 through 2025 before transitioning to a backup role in 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: The Dutch-Belgian driver competes for Red Bull Racing and has claimed four consecutive world championships between 2021 and 2024. Across his 12 seasons in Formula One, he has secured 71 Grand Prix victories.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu, the sole Chinese driver to have competed in Formula One, raced in the series from 2022 through 2024. He currently holds a reserve driver position with Cadillac in Formula One.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based team has competed as Alpine since 2021, adopting the name of Renault's sports car brand while maintaining its role as the manufacturer's official works outfit. Originally known as Renault F1 Team and backed by Groupe Renault, the squad operated under Alpine branding until Renault's withdrawal from the sport at the conclusion of 2025.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin has contested Formula One racing under multiple guises throughout its history, with the current incarnation operating as AMR GP Limited under the Aston Martin Aramco branding in the championship.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of the Italian luxury automaker, holds the distinction of being both the longest-active and most accomplished team in Formula One history, with an uninterrupted presence in the championship since its inception in 1950. The squad, colloquially termed "the Prancing Horse" after its emblematic symbol, remains a cornerstone institution of the sport.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: Gene Haas founded this American Formula One outfit in 2014, launching competitive operations in 2016 with an ambitious entry into the sport. Leadership transitioned in early 2024 when Ayao Komatsu assumed the principal role from long-serving Guenther Steiner, who had overseen the team since its establishment.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: The Swiss Sauber operation, established in 1970 by Peter Sauber, initially built sports cars and achieved endurance racing success including Le Mans victory before transitioning to Formula One in 1993. Throughout three decades of grand prix competition, the independent constructor underwent numerous transformations before ceasing operations in 2025 as one of the sport's longest-serving teams by race entries. Audi acquired the team and its infrastructure in 2024 to establish its own championship programme.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing is a British Formula One team headquartered in Woking that operates as a subsidiary of the McLaren Group under Mumtalakat Holding Company ownership. The team competes in the sport from its base at the McLaren Technology Centre.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has maintained a continuous presence in Formula One since 1954, functioning as both a constructor and engine supplier. The current team, based in Brackley and operating under a German licence, became a tripartite venture in 2022 with equal ownership stakes held by Mercedes-Benz Group, Ineos, and team principal Toto Wolff. The squad is traditionally identified by the "Silver Arrows" designation.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that began competing in 2024 as part of Red Bull's two-team operation. Based in Faenza with an additional facility near Milton Keynes, the squad functions as a sister outfit to Red Bull Racing under Austrian ownership.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that entered the championship in 2024 as part of Red Bull's two-team operation. Based in Faenza with facilities near its Milton Keynes sister team, the squad competes alongside Red Bull Racing under Austrian conglomerate Red Bull's ownership.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Red Bull Racing, an Austrian-licensed Formula One team headquartered in England, has been owned by the Red Bull conglomerate since its 2005 establishment. Christian Horner led the team through two decades of competition before Laurent Mekies assumed the principal role in 2025. Red Bull GmbH also operates a second Formula One entry through Racing Bulls.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering, operating as Atlassian Williams F1 Team in 2026, is a British Formula One constructor established in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head following the collapse of Williams's prior racing venture. Based at a substantial facility in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team has been a significant force in the sport's history.
